item.title: Iran tried to assassinate one of Netanyahu's sons, prime minister says
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu claims Iran tried to murder one of his sons, urging enhanced protection for prime ministerial candidates during the election campaign.

item.title: Hormuz crisis hides a deeper oil threat that could outlast the war
item.description: Art Berman warns that 8 million barrels shut in near the Strait of Hormuz may never fully recover, even after a ceasefire reopens the waterway.

item.title: Woman in her 30s who pretended to be a child and lived with family found guilty of fraud
item.description: Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira, 37, lived with a family as their daughter for 14 months before her elaborate child identity fraud was uncovered.

item.title: Dominican Republic joins global fight against antisemitism with landmark move
item.description: Rabbi Yehuda Kaploun called the Dominican Republic's IHRA adoption a "historic moment" and urged other Latin American governments to follow suit.

item.title: Watchdog demands apology after UN memorial erroneously honors Hamas terrorist
item.description: UN Watch says UNRWA teacher Imad Youssif El Samhouri glorified terrorism for years before the United Nations honored him at a memorial service.

item.title: Could Iran’s regime collapse? Experts assess Bessent’s bid to sever financial lifelines
item.description: Scott Bessent's "Economic D-Day" against Iran sent the rial to an all-time low as experts debate whether maximum pressure can trigger regime change.

item.title: Denmark's left-wing PM warns: 'Big enemy has started to grow from within' as Europe faces migrant reckoning
item.description: Mette Frederiksen's stance on Denmark immigration and border control puts her at odds with Spain's PM, as she names failed integration and Islamist extremism as key threats.
